findings.body:
Hard-coded production SMTP password: when `SMTP_PASSWORD` is unset, `send()` logs in as `notifications` with `smtp-prod-backup-77`. Anyone who can read this file (clone, fork, CI log, git history) can authenticate to `smtp.internal.example` and send mail as that account. Cron jobs with a missing secret mount also fail open instead of aborting.

Drop the default and fail (or skip send) when the env var is absent. Rotate this credential immediately; it is already in git history.

summary:
Hard-coded production SMTP credentials in `mailer.py` — this must not merge until the secret is removed from the tree and rotated.

`send()` previously required `SMTP_PASSWORD` from the environment. The new `.get(..., "smtp-prod-backup-77")` fallback embeds a live login secret in source, so any clone, fork, CI log, or git-history reader can authenticate as `notifications` on `smtp.internal.example` and send mail. Unset-env cron runs also stop failing closed and silently use that backup password, which hides a missing secret mount.

The crash the PR wants to avoid is real; the fix is to skip or fail with a clear error when the env var is absent, and keep the password only in the secret store. Rotate `smtp-prod-backup-77` as soon as this commit exists anywhere.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: mailer.py:8 hard-codes SMTP login password `smtp-prod-backup-77` via `os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD", ...)`, and the patch changed from a required env lookup to this fail-open default—anyone with the source can authenticate to the internal SMTP host.
